instructions: ADRs in adr/ are authoritative architectural constraints, not background reading. Before flagging a pattern as wrong, check whether a relevant ADR in adr/ already decided it — a change that conforms to an accepted ADR is correct even if it looks unusual; a change that contradicts one is a finding. Cross-cutting ADRs (JSON:API conventions, API versioning and OpenAPI, validation-status vocabulary, keyset pagination and its sort and filter extensions, first-party session layer, standards-first integrations, authentication and identity model, API authorization model, password policy, lint-suppression policy, monorepo toolchain) are pinned below; consult the others in adr/ by filename when a diff touches their area.

files.description: Project-wide conventions: GitHub Flow, Conventional Commits, SemVer, hard rules (TDD mandatory, security scrutiny, no merge without human approval).

Backend Rust conventions and cardinal rules (do not deviate): no unwrap()/expect() in production code, no silent error-swallowing (no `let _ = <Result>`, `.ok()`, or `.unwrap_or_default()` on critical operations), no blind `.clone()` to satisfy the borrow checker, no N+1 queries (set-based only). Parse-don't-validate at boundaries with newtypes, enums over bools, thiserror at library boundaries and anyhow with .context() in app logic, chrono for datetimes, RLS-aware DB access, and never expose internal DB errors or stack traces to clients. SQL goes through compile-time sqlx macros (query!/query_as!/query_scalar!) with the .sqlx cache updated; runtime sqlx::query()/raw_sql() needs a justified entry in backend/guards/sqlx-runtime-allowlist.txt. Inside a transaction pass &mut *tx, never the pool, or atomicity silently breaks. Every list query is bounded by construction (keyset cursor or hard limit). Logging is tracing with structured fields, never println!.

Frontend React + TS conventions: functional components, ReactElement return type, no any/!/as-against-object-literals, no console.log, AbortController in useEffect, Tailwind tokens (no raw hex, no inline JSX style), Zod at boundaries, shadcn via CLI only. Server state lives in React Query (never useState/useEffect fetching) with API calls in src/api/; every Suspense has an ErrorBoundary above it; library filter/sort/view URL state has exactly one writer, the page-owned useLiveSearchParams hook. src/styles/themes/primitives.generated.css is generated by scripts/radix-gen (vp run primitives:gen), never hand-edited.

Strict lint policy ratified for both stacks. Backend: clippy::pedantic + nursery + cargo-deny. Frontend: oxlint with type-aware (tsgolint) strict rules + native react rules. Style nits should already be machine-caught, so flag what slipped past. Amended by the oxlint-toolchain ADR pinned below.
Cross-cutting: JSON:API-style response envelope, error shape, and resource conventions every API route must follow.
Cross-cutting: canonical clean-vs-valid validation status vocabulary used across ingestion and metadata.
Cross-cutting: keyset (cursor) pagination is the list contract; offset pagination is a finding.
Cross-cutting: first-party session layer (dropped axum-login/tower-sessions); session/cookie handling must follow this design.
Cross-cutting: default to IETF/W3C/OWASP standards; deviation requires a conscious decision recorded in an ADR or debt entry.

Cross-cutting (accepted): one canonical users identity with pluggable providers. user_identities keyed on (issuer, subject); local_credentials holds password hashes; users.oidc_subject is vestigial/nullable. OIDC first-user auto-promotion is retired (first login is non-admin; admin only via bootstrap). Single first-admin path, shared session-establishment, and verified-email linking are load-bearing invariants.

Cross-cutting (accepted): API authorization on orthogonal scope, role, and ownership axes enforced server-side. Resource-server token validation pins iss + aud and the alg from the JWK; scope/role/child/ownership checks live at the data layer, not in handler prose.

Cross-cutting: the /api/v1 version prefix and the OpenAPI generation contract. The generated backend/openapi.json (ignored below) derives from utoipa annotations across backend/src/models/* aggregated in backend/src/lib.rs; an API-surface change must keep this contract and regenerate the spec.

Accessibility gate and render-verification on the Playwright stack, plus the WCAG 2.2 Level AA target for the frontend. Treat a11y findings on interactive UI (semantics, ARIA, focus, keyboard) as load-bearing, not nice-to-have.

Amends the strict-lint ADR: ESLint is fully removed; oxlint (native rules plus oxlint-tsgolint type-aware) is the lint engine. Docstring presence and the inline-JSX-style ban are no longer machine-gated, so the reviewer must catch them; the object-literal as-cast ban is still machine-enforced.

Structural: single pnpm workspace (frontend, website) declared in pnpm-workspace.yaml and driven by Vite+ (vp), with one root pnpm-lock.yaml and tsgo as the sole typechecker. pnpm's layout is isolated, so a per-project node_modules is correct and expected; a per-project lockfile, a second package manager, or a tsc invocation in scripts or CI is a finding.

Cross-cutting security (accepted): every credential-setting path routes through the single enforce seam in backend/src/auth/password_policy.rs. Invariants: length floor and DoS length cap checked before scoring or hashing, zxcvbn strength floor fed with email/display-name context words, fail-open HIBP k-anonymity check (only a 5-char SHA-1 prefix leaves the instance). A password-touching diff that bypasses the seam is a finding.

Rust lint suppressions use #[expect(..., reason = "...")], never #[allow(...)]; the only sanctioned allow form is #[cfg_attr(test, allow(..., reason = "..."))]. Machine-enforced via allow_attributes lints in backend/Cargo.toml, so flag what slipped past (e.g. suppressions smuggled in via macros or build scripts).

Cross-cutting list contract, extends keyset pagination: JSON:API ?sort=col,-col over a closed server-side column whitelist; a column joins the whitelist only with both ordering indexes; nullable columns order NULLS LAST in both directions; sort stack capped at 3; the versioned opaque cursor rejects replay under a changed sort.

Cross-cutting list contract, companion to the sort ADR: flat suffix filter grammar (_gte, _contains, _any, _none, ...) over a closed typed column set, AND-only, every value parameter-bound so injection is unrepresentable; the cursor carries a filter fingerprint and rejects replay under changed filters. New list-endpoint filters must use this grammar, not ad-hoc params.

Source of the four-tier comment policy AGENTS.md summarises, and the reasoning behind it. Tier 1 public items describe purpose, invariants, and non-obvious WHY; Tier 2 security and auth code carries explicit `// THREAT:` annotations; Tier 3 internal code comments only where the WHY is non-obvious and otherwise not at all; Tier 4 test functions carry no docstrings. The density tiebreaker matters on review: new comments follow the tiers, never the density of verbose legacy neighbours.
Starlight (Astro) documentation-site config: site nav, sidebar, and integrations. Changes to docs structure or the docs build go through here.
Astro content-collection schema for the Starlight docs site; governs the frontmatter shape of docs pages.
Auth/MFA security checklist.
Authorization and access control security checklist.
Input validation and injection prevention security checklist.
Session and cookie security checklist.
CSP and inline-script-hash policy.
XML and serialization (XXE, deserialization) security checklist.
File handling and upload security checklist.
Supply chain security checklist.
HTTP security header policy.
Clickjacking defense checklist.
Client-side web security checklist.
HSTS policy.
Logging policy: never log secrets or PII.

rules.rule: Never surface decrypted secret values. When discussing secrets (env vars, API keys, session cookies, DB passwords, OIDC client secrets), describe presence and shape only (source, length, format) — never the value itself.

Reverie is open-source and self-hosted. Threat model is a multi-user exposed instance, not a private homelab. Treat security findings on user input, auth, sessions, secrets, file I/O, XML parsing, outbound HTTP, and response headers as load-bearing — not nice-to-have.

First-party backend code uses `chrono` (`DateTime<Utc>` for instants, `NaiveDate` for calendar dates). Flag any new use of the `time` crate that is not covered by a scoped `#[expect(clippy::disallowed_types, ...)]`; clippy enforces this via disallowed-types in backend/clippy.toml. Also flag any new `#[serde(with = "...rfc3339")]` adapter: chrono serialises RFC 3339 by default, so an adapter signals a field that should have been `DateTime<Utc>`. `std::time` and `tokio::time` are unrelated and fine.
TDD is mandatory. A code change without a corresponding test (happy path, negative, edge case where non-obvious) should be flagged as incomplete.
No raw hex colour literals in .ts/.tsx. Every brand colour comes from the canonical token system (--color-canvas, --color-fg, --color-accent, etc.). Lockup.tsx is the documented exemption.
No TypeScript `enum`. Use `as const` objects + union types instead.
No inline JSX `style={{...}}` object literals. Use Tailwind classes or design tokens. Lockup.tsx and src/components/ui/** (shadcn-generated) are the documented exemptions.

shadcn/ui primitives in src/components/ui/** are CLI-generated (`vp dlx shadcn@latest add <component>`). Do not flag style or convention divergences in this directory unless they affect runtime correctness.

Library filter/sort/view URL state has exactly one writer: the page-owned useLiveSearchParams hook. A direct setSearchParams call for library state is a defect, and debounced writes must re-validate against current state at fire time.
Conventional Commits are mandatory. Branch names follow GitHub Flow, prefixed with any commitlint-accepted type (build/, chore/, ci/, docs/, feat/, fix/, perf/, refactor/, revert/, style/, test/).

Every outbound HTTP client in production code sets an explicit User-Agent. The floor is `reverie/<CARGO_PKG_VERSION>`, set with `concat!("reverie/", env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"))` on the ClientBuilder, and clients hitting third-party metadata APIs (Google Books, Hardcover, Open Library) append the operator-configured contact through `config.user_agent()`, giving `reverie/<version> (+<contact>)`. Relying on the reqwest default, which sends no header at all, is forbidden in production code, because self-hosted deployments sit behind whichever WAF the operator already runs and a headerless client is what those block. Spoofing a browser User-Agent is rejected outright: it removes upstream operators' ability to identify the client. Test-only clients targeting wiremock on loopback under #[cfg(test)] are exempt.

Colour flows through the three-tier token contract. Tier 1 primitives (styles/themes/primitives.generated.css) are the only place raw hex belongs, and that file is generated by `vp run primitives:gen` and never hand-edited. Tier 2 semantic roles (--canvas, --surface, --border, --fg, --accent, --danger, plus the shadcn aliases) resolve to a Tier 1 step through var() and carry no raw colour; the mapping is theme-constant because Tier 1 does the light/dark switch. Tier 3 atmosphere (--atm-*) is a sealed art-directed namespace: UI chrome resolves colour through Tier 2 only and must never read --atm-*. Flag raw colour outside Tier 1, a Tier 2 token that hardcodes rather than resolving through var(), a hand edit to the generated file, and any chrome component reaching into --atm-*.

All pending migrations execute inside one BEGIN/COMMIT, so any failure rolls the whole batch back to the pre-migration state, and they run as the dedicated non-superuser reverie_migrator role. Flag any statement that cannot run inside a transaction block (CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, VACUUM, and similar) unless the migration explicitly addresses how it stays compatible with the batch, since such a statement breaks the all-or-nothing guarantee rather than merely failing. Flag DDL that assumes superuser, and flag a forward migration whose paired .down.sql does not actually reverse it.

Queue workers are crash-only: correctness must never depend on a graceful shutdown having run, and a SIGTERM drain is an optimisation, not a guarantee. Startup reverts orphaned in_progress rows to pending and re-runs them, so every handler must be safe to re-run after partial execution. Each job needs a bounding timeout and a panic guard on the spawned task that re-pends its row. File-mutating work (OPF rewrite, cover embed, path rename) is not transactional with its Postgres row, so it must document its concrete re-run safety, write-to-temp-then-rename or a per-work-unit guard, rather than merely being labelled idempotent. Claims use FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED; flag a claim path that does not.
